HelpAudioCodec: AC3 and E-AC3 are Dolby Digital. AAC is universal.
HelpAudioLanguage: Only include content whose default audio track is this language, such as English only or Japanese only. Leave it empty to keep every language.
HelpBackground: A solid box is the most readable over bright scenes.
HelpCategory: Tags the whole channel in the guide. Kids is set per rating block, and the movie tag is applied automatically while a movie is playing.
HelpContent: This channel will contain content from the libraries configured below.
HelpCopyMatchingVideo: Sends an item's video as it is, with no encoding, when it is already in the Video Codec, SDR, and no larger than the Resolution. A copied item keeps its own size, frame rate, and bitrate.
HelpDefaultLanguage: Your native language. A channel set to Forced only burns in subtitles when its audio is in another language, so foreign content stays followable.
HelpDisableHardwareAcceleration: Forces software encoding and decoding. Turn this on if channels fail to play with hardware acceleration.
HelpEnablePopular: Disable to hide it without affecting your own channels.
HelpEpisodesPerBlock: Consecutive episodes per series before moving on. 1 disables grouping.
HelpFavorContentType: Weights one type more heavily in the loop, repeating it to fill the share if needed.
HelpGeneratedLogoStyle: Used when no image is uploaded.
HelpIncludeMovies: Tagged in the guide while a movie is playing.
HelpKeepMultipart: Keeps two part episodes together across a block boundary.
HelpLogoSymbol: Any Material Symbols name, drawn in the centre. Browse names at fonts.google.com/icons.
HelpLogoUpload: Upload a custom square logo for this channel. With no upload, the preview shows the generated logo.
HelpLoopOrder: How the channel arranges its content. Chronological plays oldest to newest by release date.
HelpMaxConcurrentStreams: Most channels that may encode at once. The oldest is closed to make room, and 0 means no limit.
HelpMinCommunityRating: Only include content rated at least this by the audience, on a 0 to 10 scale, like 7.5 for a best-of channel. 0 allows everything. Content with no community rating is dropped.
HelpMinCriticRating: Only include content with at least this critic score, on a 0 to 100 scale. 0 allows everything. Content with no critic rating is dropped.
HelpOutlineColor: Used for the outline, or for the box behind the text.
HelpPeople: Limit the channel to content featuring these people, like a favourite director or actor. Search by name to add. Leave empty to allow everyone.
HelpPlaceholderBlocks: A placeholder block takes the channel off air for its window. The guide shows one program by the block's Guide Name and the channel loops a card with your message. Whatever is airing when the window opens is cut there, and the loop goes on when it ends.
HelpPlaceholderCustom: The Custom style plays an image, GIF, or video from a path on the server. A GIF or video loops cleanly when it is exactly 10 seconds and ends where it starts, and its sound is not played. In the message, {time} becomes the time the channel resumes and {contentName} what it resumes with. Leave the title or message empty to leave it off.
HelpPopularIcon: Any Material Symbols name, drawn in the centre of the generated logo. Browse names at fonts.google.com/icons.
HelpPopularRatingBlocks: Limit which ratings air, optionally by time of day. No blocks means anything airs. On overlap, the lowest min and max win. The top titles are picked from what the rating allows.
HelpRatingBlocks: Limit which ratings air, optionally by time of day. No blocks means anything airs. On overlap, the lowest min and max win.
HelpResetSchedule: Rebuilds every channel schedule, the guide, and every channel's buffer cards from your current settings. Use it to clear a stale schedule, like after changing a channel's genres or filters.
HelpResolution: Every item is scaled to this one fixed size.
HelpShowUpNextCards: Plays a 10 second card before each item showing its artwork, title, episode and rating. The card is part of the item's time in the guide, so the item still starts on schedule.
HelpSources: A Collection source plays every item in the collection, with series expanded to their episodes. Whitelist plays only the picked items and Blacklist plays everything else. Search a show, movie, episode, music video, or home video by name to pick it.
HelpStreamFileLocation: Where playlists and segments are written while playing, taking effect on restart. Blank uses Jellyfin's cache. Pick a new or empty folder. The plugin cleans up old stream files inside this folder automatically, so it refuses one that already contains other content.
HelpStreamTimeLimit: Closes a stream open longer than this once no one is watching it. 0 turns it off.
HelpStressTest: Finds how many streams this server can encode at once using the real channel pipeline. Each round encodes a minute of the test item with one more stream than the last, until a stream drops below 30 fps. That count is your Maximum Concurrent Streams. It runs for a few minutes, loads the server heavily, and needs all channel streams stopped first.
HelpStudios: Limit the channel to these studios or networks, like an HBO channel. Leave empty to allow all. For shows this also matches the series' studio.
HelpSubtitleAppearance: How burned-in subtitles look on every channel. Leave everything untouched to render each subtitle as it was authored, with its own bold, italic, and color tags.
HelpSubtitleBurnIn: Bakes subtitles into the picture for everyone. Forced only burns the forced track, or the full track when the audio is in another language, while Always burns them on everything.
HelpSubtitleFont: A font family installed on the server, such as Arial.
HelpSubtitleSize: A percentage of normal. 100 keeps the size the subtitle was authored at.
HelpTestItem: Search for one movie or episode to test with. Something demanding like 4K or HDR gives the most honest number. This choice is not saved.
HelpTextColor: As Authored keeps each subtitle's own color.
HelpTransitionWindow: Items starting this close to a window change must fit both windows. Set it to your longest content. 0 turns it off.
HelpVideoCodec: HEVC is smaller but less compatible. The encoder follows your Jellyfin hardware acceleration.
HelpYears: Limit the channel to certain production years, like a 90s channel. Enter years and ranges separated by commas, for example 1990-1999 or 1985, 1999, 2003. Leave blank to allow every year. For shows this uses each episode's year, so a long-running series contributes only its episodes from those years.

PopularIntro: A ready made channel at number 0 that loops the recent, top rated, and most watched movies and shows on your server. It works with no setup, and everything here lets you rename it, change its icon, cap its rating, and tune how it loops.
SessionsIntro: Every channel encoding on the server, with how fast it transcodes, where 1.0x keeps up with realtime. Select a session to read or copy its ffmpeg log, or to kill the stream.
SettingsIntro: Output and playback options that apply to every channel, including the Popular one. Set the resolution, codecs, and bitrate, then open a section to adjust hardware, playback, and session limits.
TaskCleanChannelsDirectoryDescription: Removes leftover Live Channels stream directories that are no longer tied to an active channel, in case one got stuck or was not cleared on close.
TaskGenerateBufferCardsDescription: Renders the tune-in card, the shared Up Next layer and the placeholder cards of every enabled Live Channels channel that does not have current ones, so tuning in never waits on a render, an Up Next card only adds the item, and a placeholder only adds its message.
TitleExportChannels: Export all channels to a file
